1: This era starts where the map does, with the fall of the Jerusalem Temple in 70 CE. It runs to Constantine's Edict of Milan in 313, which gave Christians, and all others, freedom to follow the religion they chose. The Persian church east of Rome had the opposite experience. Persecution there grew worse after 312.
2: Historians call this the era of the 'imperial church'. Christianity moves from a persecuted minority to the empire's own religion. Its defining creeds, from Nicaea to Chalcedon, are settled because an emperor now has a stake in the outcome.
3: In this era the churches part into separate communions. Chalcedonian, miaphysite and East Syriac Christianity become distinct families, each with a sense of its own identity. The Latin West enters the post-Roman kingdoms. Monasticism becomes the force that shapes it everywhere.
4: Christianity becomes a minority faith across its old heartlands as Islam rises. It converts new peoples in the north and fights an internal war over religious images. It sends its longest missions east along the Silk Road.
5: In the Latin West, new religious orders and new lay movements appear. Women's religious life grows to a scale not seen before. Byzantium consolidates, and the Christian East comes under new pressures.
6: Plague, papal schism and institutional crisis mark this era. They are met by devotional writing more inward than any before it, and more often in everyday languages for lay people to read. The Black Death sweeps Europe from 1347 to 1351.
7: The Western church is remade, several ways at once. This era holds the Reformation's many movements, often rivals, side by side. Most have direct descendants still living today.
8: Established churches settle into place. Renewal moves into small groups, personal religious experience and revivals on both sides of the Atlantic. In this era, the spiritual life story told in the first person becomes a mass genre.
9: Christianity spreads around the world, both under empire and against it. Mission is tangled with colonialism, revival with respectability, and liberation with paternalism. None of these pairs is resolved in this era.
10: Christianity's center of gravity moves south and east. The Pentecostal and Spirit-movement family becomes the largest new form of Christianity since the Reformation. World War I (1914–18) breaks out early in this era.
